$schemaNote: Fault-family cells for ProofRequirementKind.QualifierCompatibility. Each cell carries the discharge contract (iff + decision procedure), the transport-rule citation with the citation duty on any declared fact it consumes, and a witness triple (base -> reject / discharge-addition -> clean / near-miss -> reject-same-obligation). Every .precept snippet was syntax/compile-validated through the precept MCP (precept_compile) at HEAD on 2026-07-21; the recorded diagnostic codes and obligation dispositions are compile-oracle OBSERVATIONS of the shipped compiler, never cited as authority for what the DEFINITION says. Known compiler holes checked against every witness: BUG-033 (dequeue/pop `into` target not registered as a write site) and the un-build-enforced write-surface enumeration — no witness here rests on either (no snippet writes an operand field via an `into` target or across an exit-hook kill), so no cell is flagged for a hole. Grounded against: src/Precept/Language/Operations.cs (QualifierCompatibilityProofRequirement mint sites), src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.cs:305-307 (bin.ProofRequirements instantiation), src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.Qualifiers.cs (TryQualifierCompatibilityProof / QualifiersAreCompatible — declaration discharge), src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.QualifierNarrowing.cs (TryQualifierGuardNarrowingProof / NarrowedValueFromGuard — guard discharge), src/Precept/Language/ProofRequirement.cs:113-118 (the DU subtype), docs/Working/obligation-discharge-matrix-2026-07-19.md (rev 7 — fault case shape, citation-duty ruling, minting rule), docs/Working/transport-rule-restatement-2026-07-21.md (route index over the 23-value evaluation-site axis).

mintSite.fileLine: src/Precept/Language/Operations.cs (dual-subject QualifierCompatibilityProofRequirement on BinaryOperationMeta.ProofRequirements — QualifierAxis.Currency for money±money, QualifierAxis.Unit for quantity±quantity, and BOTH .Unit and .Currency for price±price)
mintSite.howMinted: catalog-declared on BinaryOperationMeta.ProofRequirements; instantiated per occasion at ProofEngine.cs:305-307 (`foreach (var req in bin.ProofRequirements) obligations.Add(new ProofObligation(req, bin, ctx, Unresolved, ...))`) whenever WalkExpression visits a TypedBinaryOp on a business-domain magnitude pair. Keyed by occasion, not syntactic position (minting rule, site-identity ruling 2026-07-21): one written `+` reached by N routes mints N obligations, each proved from its own route's facts.
mintSite.notCatalogEnumeratedButRelated: price±price mints TWO QualifierCompatibility obligations (Unit and Currency) from one binary op (Operations.cs PricePlusPrice/PriceMinusPrice); the cells below use money±money (single Currency-axis obligation) as the representative business-domain witness and note the price double-obligation where it changes the count.

inapplicable.(d) pre-state constraint / inductive hyp: N/A for this kind. A qualifier axis value is not a preservable runtime quantity: a DECLARED qualifier (`in 'USD'`, `of 'kg'`) is immutable declaration metadata — no write site can change field F's declared currency/unit, because any `set F = e` to a qualified field re-mints its OWN qualifier-compat obligation to keep the axis value invariant (Operations.cs assignment path). An OPEN field's runtime currency is a value, but no qualifier obligation carries it as a pre-state constraint fact — the engine tracks it only through the guard-narrowing (class c) and declaration (class a/b) surfaces. So there is no class-(d) fact to consume, and the citation duty for class (d) never arises here.

premiseClasses.note: The fault-case discharge column in the matrix (§ Per-family case shapes) reads classes (b)/(c)/(a); (d) is admitted family-wide under the 2026-07-21 citation duty but is vacuous for the qualifier axis per the row above. Class (a) is NOT exempt from the citation duty (2026-07-21 ruling) — a field's declared qualifier is a one-field constraint whose truth at the site must be named; here its establishing obligation is the declaration and its preserving-obligation set is EMPTY (see per-cell citationDuty).

dischargeMechanics.decisionProcedureShared: A QualifierCompatibilityProofRequirement(L, R, axis A) at binary-op site s discharges IFF resolve(L,A,s) and resolve(R,A,s) are both defined AND QualifiersAreCompatible(resolve(L,A,s), resolve(R,A,s), A) (ProofEngine.Qualifiers.cs:118-173), where resolve(operand,A,s) = [1] the operand field/arg's DECLARED qualifier on axis A if it declares one — premise class (a) for a field, (b) for an event arg (ResolveQualifierFromExpression / ResolveQualifierOnAxis); else [2] the guard-narrowed value v if the enclosing context's guard provably pins the operand's field to a single value v on A across EVERY disjunctive branch AND the field is not in obligation.ReassignedBefore — premise class (c) (TryQualifierGuardNarrowingProof / NarrowedValueFromGuard, ProofEngine.QualifierNarrowing.cs:96-170); else [3] undefined -> reject (PRE0114). Compatibility (QualifiersAreCompatible): equal value, or symbolically equal via shared SourceFieldName / source path (interpolated `in '{CurrencyCode}'` on both operands), or same dimension name across Unit/Dimension subtypes, or CompoundPrice component-wise (currency AND unit) match.
dischargeMechanics.searchBound: Finite and search-free: one declaration lookup per operand; when an operand is open, a finite structural scan of the enclosing guard's conjunction/disjunction tree (ExtractQualifierNarrowingBranches) requiring all-branch agreement to a single value; then a finite string/structural compatibility test. No interval arithmetic, no fixpoint. Bounded by the guard's syntactic size.
dischargeMechanics.rejectSide: resolve undefined on either operand (open with no narrowing guard, or a guard that narrows to a mismatched value / fails all-branch agreement) OR compatible-check false -> PRE0114, naming both operands and their resolved-or-unresolved axis values, suggesting `Align both declarations, or insert an explicit conversion`.

transportShared.declaredQualifierFact: For a class-(a) field-modifier or class-(b) arg qualifier: the fact `F.<axis> == v` is established by the qualifier DECLARATION and is carried at route position zero. Its read-closure deps is empty — a declared qualifier is immutable metadata, so mayWrite(r,p,q) never intersects it and the fact is NEVER killed on any route reaching the site (transport-rule-restatement § What kills — guards/conditions/modifier expressions write nothing; and the declared axis value is not a slot a `set` can change). Transport therefore holds trivially on every route in the site's route set.
transportShared.guardNarrowedFact: For a class-(c) guard fact narrowing an OPEN operand field F: the fact `F.<axis> == v` is earned at the guard (phase 2, transport § 5 'Fired-guard fact') and is KILLED by any write to F before the site — deps(φ) = {F}, and the transport premise deps(φ) ∩ mayWrite(r,p,q) = ∅ is exactly what the shipped code enforces via `obligation.ReassignedBefore.Contains(field)` (ProofEngine.QualifierNarrowing.cs:142). Route relation per occasion below.
transportShared.knownHole: If an operand field F were instead written by `dequeue C into F` / `pop C into F` between the guard and the site, BUG-033 (the `into` target not registered as a write site) would leave the guard fact wrongly alive and PRE0114 wrongly discharged. No witness below uses an `into` target on an operand field, so none is flagged; a variant that did would be FLAGGED, not counted as verified.

respellability.rationale: The band (sound-but-unprovable programs) for this kind is thin because compatibility is decided by finite declaration + guard lookup. A representative band member: an action chain `-> set Payment = Fee -> set Total = Payment + Fee` where Fee is `in 'USD'` and Payment is open — after the write, Payment's currency is provably USD by written-value provenance (E2, matrix § The cell), so the `+` is sound, yet the shipped narrowing reads only guards (not E2) and rejects with PRE0114. Its licensed respelling: add the row/hook guard `when Payment.currency == 'USD'` (class c) or declare `field Payment as money in 'USD'` (class a). Both are surface the author can write, so the gap costs authoring friction only — respellable: yes. Every cell inherits this family verdict; none overrides it.

Class (c) instance for this cell: the transition row's `when` guard (GuardOfContext -> TransitionRowContext.Row.Guard, QualifierNarrowing.cs:199) narrows an open operand field to a single axis value across all disjunctive branches, and that field is not reassigned earlier in the row's action chain.

citationDuty.preservingObligations: NONE — a declared currency qualifier is immutable; no write site can change Fee's currency (any `set Fee = e` re-mints its own qualifier-compat obligation to hold currency invariant). openFlags: SPEC-VS-COMPILER DISCREPANCY (route to owner): spec:1007 says a stateless `on E -> ...` handler carries no `when` guard, so premise class (c) is definitionally unavailable here. But `precept_compile` at HEAD ACCEPTS `on Allocate when Payment.currency == 'USD' -> ...` and uses the guard to narrow an open operand (QualifierCompatibility Proved). This is a compile-clean-but-spec-forbidden construct — the parser admits a guard the language spec disallows. Flagged, not used: the class-(b) discharge witness above does not rely on it. If the guard form is genuinely intended for stateless handlers, spec:1007 needs correcting and class (c) becomes available for this cell; if not, the parser needs to reject it. Either way it is a definition question for the owner, not resolvable in a cell.

The rule's `when` guard fact is earned where the guard evaluates and consumed at the condition site.

cells.dischargeContract: Discharges IFF the shared decision procedure resolves and matches both operands. Class (a) instance (witness below): both operand fields declare the same axis value. Class (c) instance: the rule's `when` guard (GuardOfContext -> ConstraintContext -> RuleIdentity -> semantics.Rules[i].Guard, QualifierNarrowing.cs:202-204) narrows an open operand — CONFIRMED to discharge the INNER combination obligation (see openFlags for the enclosing-comparison limitation).
cells.enclosingObligationNote: A `rule` condition must be boolean, so a money±money combination sits inside a comparison (`<= '1000 USD'`), and that enclosing money comparison co-mints a SECOND QualifierCompatibility obligation (the sum's result vs the literal). Both are the same schema at sibling sites; a fully-clean discharge requires BOTH cleared, which the class-(a) witness does (all three currencies USD). A single-obligation rejecting witness is not constructible for this occasion — any rejecting money-combination inside a boolean comparison yields the inner + enclosing pair (both fail whenever the sum's currency is unresolved).

openFlags: GUARD DISCHARGE DOES NOT PROPAGATE TO THE ENCLOSING COMPARISON (observation, not a definition gap the cell invents): with a class-(c) guard `rule Payment + Fee <= '1000 USD' when Payment.currency == 'USD'` (QC4disc), the shipped compiler PROVES the inner `+` obligation (guard narrowing narrows Payment -> USD) but leaves the enclosing `<=` obligation Unresolved, because the narrowed operand currency is not propagated into the money-combination's RESULT currency (`(Payment + Fee)` stays 'unresolved'). So a money+money inside a rule/ensure comparison, with an open operand, is not fully dischargeable by a guard alone in the shipped compiler — it must be closed by declaration (class a). Whether the definition SHOULD propagate a narrowed operand currency to a combination result (making class-(c) guard discharge sufficient for the whole condition) is a proof-power question for the owner; recorded, not resolved. The class-(a) witness above is unaffected.
